FOXP1 is itself a target of multiple compounds, including 2-hexulosonic acid and (3S,5S,8S,9S,10R,13R,14S,16S)-3,16-dihydroxy-10,13-dimethyl-1,2,3,4,5,7,8,9,11,12,14,15,16,17-tetradecahydrocyclopenta[a]phenanthren-6-one. These compounds are also targets of Tilmicosin, indicating a complex network of interactions. The final scores from the paths suggest a plausible, though not fully elucidated, pathway where Tilmicosin may modulate FOXP1, which in turn affects KvD3. The evidence supports a mechanistic link, but the exact nature of the interaction remains unclear, requiring further experimental validation. The presence of multiple targets along the pathway highlights the complexity of the relationship, and the integration of these findings may provide insight into the drug's potential therapeutic effects.
